Removed the old v1 bare-presence SOURCE fact (`zone:'Battlefield', subject:'self'`) — a real violation of the standing 'no presence in sources, only zone movements' rule (same class as Summon: Bahamut's own deleted `self-battlefield`), replaced with real `self-cast`/`self-enters` facts (both exempted via `isActivationCostPermanentBaselineFact`, tautological given `card.activationCost` is set for Crew, same as magitek-armor/the-prima-vista/the-lunar-whale).

Bare printed keywords (Flying, Vigilance) get NO fact per the 2026-09-12 standing rule — neither is self-only-and-event-producing the way Lifelink's CR 702.15e lifegain is (the one carved-out exception), both are purely passive/no-observable-occurrence.

Restricted mana ability (`{T}: Add {C}. Spend this mana only to cast an artifact spell or activate an ability of an artifact source.`) modeled as a REAL, executable named ability (`CardDefinition.abilities`, cost `{T}`, `effects:[{kind:'addMana', color:'C', amount:1}]`) — checked the pool first for a restricted-mana precedent (Freya Crescent/fin-138 and The Emperor of Palamecia/fin-219 are the only other 2 real restricted-mana abilities in FIN; neither is migrated/modeled at all, no precedent to follow). Piloted for REAL in scenarios.ts (`ability:'mana'`), producing genuine `fn:'addMana'` trace evidence — no static exemption needed, unlike The Gold Saucer's own unrestricted `{T}: Add {C}.` fact (which has no Effect at all and relies on a static exemption). The RESTRICTION itself (spend only on artifact spells/abilities) is a real, documented, honest gap: this engine tracks no spendable mana pool at all (interfaces.ts's own `Player.addMana` doc comment), so nothing could constrain what the produced mana is later spent on — the `addMana` fact represents the real, basic 'taps for mana' action only, restriction noted in definition.ts's own comment and here, not represented as a separate fact/constraint (no vocabulary for it, and no real card in the pool wants it yet).

Crew 1 modeled with the same real `crewCost`+`activationCost`+`effects:[animate]` machinery Magitek Armor/The Prima Vista/The Lunar Whale already established — `event:'crew'` + `event:'grantType', type:'Creature', untilEndOfTurn:true` SOURCE facts, plus the same `{to:'Battlefield', controller:'you', types:{has:['Creature']}}` sink (wants a creature to crew it) magitek-armor already has, covered by the pre-existing `isCrewCostCreatureWant` exemption (structural — this harness's simplified crew lifecycle doesn't validate `crewedBy` power against the real requirement).

One scenario (per the task's own '1 default, real basic function only' instruction): `ability:'mana'` (real addMana trace) + `you:{creaturesCount:1}` + `sequence:[{activate:true}]` (real crew/animate trace) — both real activated-ability lifecycles demonstrated against one shared GameState, mirroring magitek-armor's own consolidated single-scenario shape.

New, previously-undocumented ENGINE_GAPS.md finding (Lower priority #11, Crew N sub-entry): `engine.ts`'s real `canActivateAbility`/`activateAbility` branch on `card.crewCost !== undefined` UNCONDITIONALLY, before checking `abilityName` — so a Vehicle with BOTH crew AND a separate named ability would have any activation attempt incorrectly routed through the crew-cost path if piloted through `engine.ts`'s real engine (not an issue for this card's own `harness.ts` flat-scenario style, which calls `resolveCard` directly and never consults `crewCost`). Cargo Ship is the first real card in the pool with this shape; documented, not fixed (out of scope for a fact-authoring pass).

Also surfaced (not fixed, pre-existing, unrelated to this migration): `factsInteract`'s event-to-event matching branch never checks a want's own `types` constraint at all (only `event`/`counterType`/`colors`/`tapped`/`target` are compared) — Ultima, Origin of Oblivion's own addMana sink declares `types:{has:['Land']}` (its blight-counter effect only affects lands) but this constraint is silently ignored, so Cargo Ship's own Artifact-sourced `addMana` fact matches it anyway (`find-synergies.mjs` shows a real 'Cargo Ship --[mana production]--> Ultima, Origin of Oblivion' line that shouldn't exist under the card's own real restriction). Pre-existing matcher gap (would already misfire against any other real addMana-C producer), not introduced by this task — flagged for the parent session, not fixed here (a matcher change is cross-card-pool-wide, out of scope for a single-card migration).

`verify-synergy.mjs` cargo-ship: OK, 0 hard failures. Full pool: 315 checked, 4 pre-existing hard failures (cecil-dark-knight-cecil-redeemed-paladin, stiltzkin-moogle-merchant, white-auracite, zack-fair) — confirmed NOT touched by this task (concurrent work from another session; `git status` shows those files modified but not by any edit in this task). `npx vitest run functional-model`: 238/238. `find-synergies.mjs` diff (cargo-ship, before = old v1 bare-presence fact / after = this migration): before 35 lines (all illegitimate 'Cargo Ship --[battlefield presence]-->X', correctly removed per the no-presence-shaped-source rule); after 145 lines (108 real 'X --[battlefield presence]--> Cargo Ship' via the new creature-crew sink matching every unconstrained creature-presence producer in the pool, ~35 real 'Cargo Ship --[enters the battlefield]-->X'/'--[moves to battlefield (from ...)]-->' via self-cast/self-enters matching entersBattlefield-shaped and zone-shaped Battlefield sinks, 1 'Cargo Ship --[mana production]--> Ultima, Origin of Oblivion' — see the matcher gap noted above). Net well-understood, same shape as magitek-armor's own 12->152 migration diff.
knownGaps: The mana ability's own restriction ("Spend this mana only to cast an artifact spell or activate an ability of an artifact source") is not modeled or enforced — this engine tracks no spendable mana pool at all (interfaces.ts's own Player.addMana doc comment), so nothing could constrain what the produced mana is later spent on. The addMana fact represents only the real, unconditional 'taps for mana' action.

Not auto-recognized as a payable mana source for another spell's own cost (mana.ts's manaAbilityColorFromStaticText/manaAbilityColorsFromStaticText both explicitly exclude any "spend only"-restricted static-ability text by design) — correct behavior given the restriction, not a bug, but means this card's own mana ability can never help pay for anything in this model even when the restriction would legally allow it.

animate/LayerSet tracks no duration (layers.ts's documented scope, pre-existing, not new to this pass) — a crewed Cargo Ship becomes a creature PERMANENTLY in this model rather than 'until end of turn'.

engine.ts's canActivateAbility/activateAbility gate ANY named-ability activation through the crewCost branch whenever card.crewCost is set, ignoring abilityName — a real, previously-undocumented gap for a Vehicle with crew AND a separate ability (this card is the first in the pool with that shape), documented in ENGINE_GAPS.md's Crew N sub-entry. Does not affect this card's own harness.ts flat-scenario trace (which bypasses engine.ts entirely), only a hypothetical future engine-piloted (runEngineScenarios) version.

factsInteract's event-to-event matching never checks a want's own `types` constraint (pre-existing synergy.ts gap, not introduced here) — causes this card's own addMana fact to incorrectly match Ultima, Origin of Oblivion's own Land-restricted addMana sink. Flagged, not fixed (cross-pool matcher change, out of scope for a single-card migration).
